cards.explanation: The answer is that they've been unfaithful to their God. The message says Israel has played the harlot against their God. That is the reason given for being told not to rejoice like the nations. Nobody wants confetti on a day like that, friends.

The answer is False. Hosea 9:2 says the threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them. Those were the places food and wine came from. It's a warning, friends, so the threshing floor and winepress will not keep feeding Israel.

The answer is Assyria. The verse says Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. Two places named, and neither one is home, friends. Home is the land of the LORD, and they won't remain in it.
The answer is False. Hosea 9:4 says their bread will be for themselves and will not enter the house of the LORD. The bread stays out, friends. The verse also says all who eat will be defiled.

The answer is Memphis. Hosea 9:6 says that even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Running doesn't change the ending in that verse, friends. Heavy, but that's what the text says.

The answer is True. Hosea 9:6 says thorns will overrun their tents. It also says their precious silver will be taken over by thistles. Thistles on the silver and thorns on the tents, friends, that's the picture.

The answer is fool. The verse says the prophet is called a fool because of the greatness of their iniquity and hostility. The one bringing the message gets the insult, friends. I've been called plenty myself, and mine were about flour on my hat.
The answer is in the house of his God. Hosea 9:8 says, "Hostility is in the house of his God!" I think it's the very place you'd expect it least, friends. So that line lands hard.

The answer is guilt. Hosea 9:9 says He will remember their guilt and punish their sins. The verse also says they have deeply corrupted themselves. It's a serious line, friends, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is that they became as detestable as what they loved. Hosea 9:10 says they became "as detestable as the thing they loved." They went to Baal-peor and consecrated themselves to Shame, friends. What they gave themselves to marked them.

The answer is True. Hosea 9:11 says Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception. I think this one hurts to read, friends. It's a heavy verse, so we'll take it slow.
The answer is True. In Hosea 9:12 the LORD says, "Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!" The woe comes when He turns away, friends. It's a sober line, and it's what the text says.

The answer is Gilgal, friends! Hosea 9:15 says, "All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them." That's a heavy line, and I think it's meant to be. The LORD says it plainly, so we let it sit.

The answer is His house. In Hosea 9:15 the LORD says, "I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds." The text says they get driven out, friends. Their deeds are the reason given.
The answer is False. Hosea 9:15 says all their leaders are rebellious. That's the opposite of faithful, friends. A pretty clear line, which helps.
The answer is fruit. Hosea 9:16 says their root is withered, so they cannot bear fruit. It ties back to the grapes and first figs in verse 10, friends. A dried-up root can't make a harvest.

The answer is that they have not obeyed Him. Hosea 9:17 says, "My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him." It's a plain statement, friends, and it comes at the very end of the message. Disobedience is the stated reason.

The answer is wanderers. Hosea 9:17 says they shall be wanderers among the nations. Back in verse 3 the warning was that Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria. This verse ends the message with that word, friends.
